verdictSummary: The product fix is correct, minimal, spec-aligned and independently re-verified: the fact it narrows on (`campaign.coopSession?.mode`) is the right one, is the repo-wide idiom for exactly this host/guest distinction, is durable on the guest side through an explicitly engineered preservation guard, and fails OPEN toward fetching so it cannot silence a host or a single-player owner. The server gate is untouched and the client error is not swallowed. Every measurable claim in the two evidence files reproduced exactly, including all seven log sha256 values. ONE required edit: the fourth unit row, which the evidence cites as the mitigation for the unexercised two-device topology, does not actually pin what it claims to pin.

requiredEdits.at: the fourth row, 'a replica panel still issues no grants request' (renders with role 'replica' AND coopMode="guest")
requiredEdits.finding: The row is not load-bearing. The precondition is `mayListGrants = isSource && coopMode !== 'guest'` (CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:121). This row sets BOTH conjuncts false - authority.role is 'replica' (so isSource is false) and coopMode is 'guest' (so the second conjunct is false). It therefore passes under EITHER half of the conjunction alone, and is behaviourally a duplicate of row 1. Delete `isSource &&` from the precondition and no row in the suite fails.
requiredEdits.whyItMatters: This is not a cosmetic test nit, because the evidence leans on this exact row as a risk mitigation. grants-403-fix-local-20260915.json nonClaims states the two-device topology was NOT run and that 'the replica row in the new test pins that path at the unit level'. As written it does not: the replica/isSource guard - the sole thing standing between a genuine two-device replica and this same 403 - has no independent coverage anywhere in the suite (this is the first connected-component test for the panel, so there is no pre-existing pin either).
requiredEdits.fix: Change that row's `coopMode` to "host" (or omit the prop entirely). Either makes the second conjunct TRUE, so the row then passes only because `isSource` is false - which is the behaviour the row claims to pin. One-word change; no product change.
requiredEdits.notARegression: EXPLICIT: this commit does not REMOVE coverage. No connected-panel test existed at the base commit. The defect is that the new pin is weaker than the evidence asserts, not that the change made anything worse.

optionalEdits.at: the guest row's comment above `waitFor`: 'Let every queued effect and microtask settle before concluding "nothing was sent" - an assertion made too early proves nothing.'
optionalEdits.finding: The comment misdescribes the mechanism. `waitFor` with a NEGATIVE assertion resolves on its first synchronous poll, so it settles nothing - it is the testing-library anti-pattern the comment believes it is avoiding. The row nevertheless genuinely detects the defect, and this is MEASURED, not assumed: red-unit.log records this row failing with 'Received number of calls: 1', which proves the mount effect's fetch is already registered before waitFor's first poll (React Testing Library flushes the mount effect inside act during `render`).
optionalEdits.whyItMatters: Low: the test works. Flagged only because comment accuracy is this commit's own stated secondary purpose (it corrects two stale comments) and because a future reader could copy the pattern into a case where the call is NOT synchronous, where it would silently prove nothing.
optionalEdits.fix: Either drop the waitFor and assert directly after render (the honest shape, since the effect has already flushed), or state the real reason: 'the mount effect flushes inside render, so a call would already be registered here.'

optionalEdits.finding: The docblock whose text this commit corrected ('Reads the campaign's grants. A refusal yields an empty set...') sits immediately above `shareAuthHeaders`, not above `fetchGrants` - the function it describes, which is eight lines further down. The misplacement is PRE-EXISTING (introduced when #1521 inserted shareAuthHeaders between the comment and its function); this commit edited the block's text in place without relocating it.
optionalEdits.whyItMatters: Low. The prose is now accurate; only its attachment point is wrong. Noted because the commit touched this exact block, so moving it would have been in-scope and free - though surgical-diff discipline also argues for leaving pre-existing placement alone.
optionalEdits.fix: Move the block to sit directly above `async function fetchGrants(`.

Console noise in a green suite.

reviewQuestions.question: Is `campaign.coopSession?.mode` the right fact, available at mount for both host and guest, and can a HOST ever have mode undefined such that the panel wrongly stops fetching? Any other mount site needing the prop?

evidence: src/types/campaign/CoopSession.ts:39 - `export type CoopSessionMode = 'host' | 'guest'`, documented at :28-38 as 'The local user's role in a co-op campaign session', which is precisely the per-browser fact the stored authority cannot supply.

It is the established repo-wide idiom for this exact discrimination, not an invention of this fix: src/components/campaign/coop/CampaignCoopRouteSurfaceConnected.tsx:55 `const coopMode = campaign?.coopSession?.mode;`, src/components/campaign/coop/CampaignCoopRouteSurface.tsx:300-302 and :370/:397, src/lib/campaign/campaignAuthority.ts:31, src/lib/campaign/coop/coopHostRegistry.ts:71, src/components/campaign/CampaignNavigation.tsx:292.

It is the same object the mount site already destructures one line away - CampaignDashboardPage.tsx:372 `matchId={getCoopMatchId(campaign.coopSession)}` - so the prop costs no new round-trip, no new state and no inference.

availableAtMount.verdict: YES for both, and durably so
guestChain: Stamped at join: useCampaignStore.actions.ts:136 `createGuestCoopSession(hostMatchId, snapshot.roomCode)` -> CoopSession.ts:113 `{ mode: 'guest', roomCode, hostMatchId }`, set into the store at :142-150.

SURVIVES the host's authoritative-state merge: campaignMirrorProjection.ts:8-24 rewrites only currentDate / finances.balance / factionStandings / updatedAt over `...campaign`, so coopSession is carried through untouched.

SURVIVES hydration of the HOST's server record - the one path that could plausibly clobber it, since the guest's campaign id equals the host's and serializeCampaign.ts:192/262 does round-trip coopSession through the server body. useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts:367-381 `preserveGuestCoopSession` exists for exactly this, and is applied on the load path at :843: when the live campaign's mode is 'guest', the loaded record's coopSession is replaced by the local one. There is even a sibling guard at :836-840 refusing to let a guest's cached copy stand.

Reviewer's note: that a dedicated preservation guard was already written for this invariant is the strongest available evidence that `coopSession.mode` is the intended per-browser truth, and that this fix is reading the fact the codebase already maintains rather than a coincidence.
availableAtMount.orderingIsSafe: No race at mount. `authority` is null until the persistence metadata has been read (CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:106-108), and `isSource` is false while it is null, so the panel issues nothing before both facts are present. The mode arrives from the campaign store, which is populated at join/create - strictly earlier than the server metadata.

hostWithUndefinedMode.verdict: CANNOT wrongly stop fetching - the guard is fail-open in the safe direction
hostWithUndefinedMode.reasoning: The precondition is `isSource && coopMode !== 'guest'` (CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:121), and the prop defaults to null at :104. `undefined !== 'guest'` and `null !== 'guest'` are both TRUE, so an absent mode PRESERVES fetching. The only way the new conjunct suppresses a fetch is an explicit literal 'guest'. A host whose coopSession were somehow absent therefore keeps its previous behaviour exactly; single-player (no coopSession at all) likewise.
hostWithUndefinedMode.pinned: Test rows 2 and 3 - 'a host-mode source panel still fetches its grants' (asserts the exact URL /api/campaigns/campaign-1/grants) and 'a single-player source panel still fetches its grants' (renders with no coopMode prop at all). Both PASSED at the base commit per red-unit.log, so they pin pre-existing behaviour rather than describing the fix.
hostWithUndefinedMode.residualRiskIsTheOtherDirection: The failure direction this shape leaves open is a GUEST whose mode is absent or wrong, which would resume fetching. See finding F1 for the one path where that can happen.

otherMountSites.verdict: NONE - no other call site needs the prop
otherMountSites.result: Exactly one JSX mount exists repo-wide: src/components/gameplay/pages/campaigns/dashboard/CampaignDashboardPage.tsx:369-373, which this commit updates. The only other references are the component's own definition/export (CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:39/101/102/167), the barrel re-export src/components/campaign/share/index.ts:3 (which no other module consumes for this symbol), and the dashboard's import at CampaignDashboardPage.tsx:12. No e2e file mounts it directly.
otherMountSites.propIsOptional: `readonly coopMode?: CoopSessionMode | null` - optional, so even a future mount site that omits it compiles and keeps the pre-fix behaviour. That is the correct default for this guard's polarity (see above).

clientErrorNotSwallowed.verdict: CONFIRMED - nothing was absorbed, hidden, caught or filtered
evidence: No try/catch, no console suppression, no error filter and no `.catch()` was added anywhere in the diff.

The pre-existing tolerance `if (!response.ok) return [];` at CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:86 is UNCHANGED by this diff (it is not in the hunk set) - it predates the fix and is a response-shape guard, not an error mask.

Mechanically the console line could not have been swallowed even if someone tried: it is emitted by CHROMIUM for the failed resource, not by application code, so no client-side catch can suppress it. The count going 4 -> 0 is therefore positive proof the request is no longer issued, not proof it was hidden.

reviewQuestions.question: D1 - the guest is left with an empty share box on a shared server. Is that acceptable under the spec, or does it warrant the owner question as recorded? (judge honesty of the statement, do not decide it)
reviewQuestions.verdict: HONESTLY STATED - the question is real, correctly scoped, and correctly routed. One under-specification worth tightening. NOT DECIDED HERE.

why: It does not claim the fix solved more than it did. The record explicitly separates what changed from what did not: 'The fix stops the guest ASKING... It does NOT change what the guest is TOLD'.

It names the concrete residual (the guest still renders the source variant because its stored authority still reads 'source') and states the reason that cannot be fixed here (deciding what a shared-server guest's authority SHOULD read is a campaign-replication design question).

It is carried identically in BOTH evidence files - the diagnosis raised it before any code was written and the fix lane re-stated it after, rather than the question appearing only once the work was done.

It correctly reports the collateral improvement without overclaiming it: the Revoke buttons are gone. VERIFIED: CampaignSharePanel.tsx:79-86 renders the Revoke button only inside `grantRow`, which is only reached via `grants.map(...)` at :156, so an empty list renders no revoke affordance. Also verified there is NO grant-ISSUING control in the panel at all (the only interactive element in the file is that one Revoke button), so the fix does not leave behind a different always-failing control that would 403 on click - a failure mode the record would otherwise have had to disclose.

underSpecification.finding: The record describes the residual as 'an empty share box'. MEASURED, the guest actually sees a heading 'Shared access' above the copy 'This campaign has not been shared.' (CampaignSharePanel.tsx:141-152, data-testid campaign-share-empty). For a guest that sentence is not merely uninformative, it is false - the campaign HAS been shared, with them, which is why they are looking at it.

An owner reading only 'empty share box' might rate the residual cosmetic; reading the literal string, they may not.
underSpecification.recommendation: Quote the literal copy in D1 when the owner picks it up. This is a documentation sharpening of an OPEN question, not a required edit to this PR.

specReading.verdict: The fix violates no SHALL; the residual sits in genuinely undecided territory - which is why deferring it is the correct call, not an evasion.
citations: campaign-replication/spec.md:5-10 - 'the source SHALL list all three active grants'. Listing is assigned to the SOURCE. No SHALL anywhere in campaign-replication grants a guest, grantee or replica the capability to LIST a campaign's grants, so removing the guest's request removes a capability the spec never conferred. The fix moves the client TOWARD the spec.

campaign-replication/spec.md:5-10 - 'A replica SHALL present itself as a replica in every surface that shows campaign identity.' This is the SHALL nearest the residual, and it does not bind here: a shared-server guest is not a replica by stored authority (it reads the host's record, role 'source'). Whether it OUGHT to be is exactly D1's question - i.e. the residual is a gap in what the spec covers, not a breach of what it says.
The route's own header, grants.ts:11-14, states the source gate 'authorizes nobody on its own' for co-op guests. The client now agrees with that sentence for the first time.
specReading.ownerRouting: design-campaign-authority-and-sync, as recorded. Correct: the surviving question is about what a shared-server guest's stored authority should read, which that change owns.
specReading.notDecidedByThisReview: EXPLICIT - this review judges only that the question is honestly stated, correctly scoped and correctly routed. It takes no position on whether a co-op guest's dashboard should render the share panel.

findings.type: pre-existing gap the fix now leans on
findings.finding: The load path at :843 wraps its hydration in `preserveGuestCoopSession(...)` so a guest keeps `mode: 'guest'` when the host's server record is read. `resolveConflictTakeServer` does NOT: it calls `writeLiveCampaign(deserializeCampaignRecord(migrated))` directly at ~:1201-1203. Since serializeCampaign.ts:192/262 round-trips coopSession through the server body, and the guest's campaign id equals the host's, a guest that resolves a save conflict by taking the server record would inherit the HOST's coopSession (mode 'host') - after which `coopMode !== 'guest'` is true again and the panel resumes issuing the 403 request.

findings.recommendation: Not an edit to this PR. Worth a follow-up to either apply preserveGuestCoopSession at the take-server site too, or to document why a guest cannot reach it. findings.finding: The chosen shape is the minimum that can work, and it is the minimum for a principled reason rather than by luck. The three candidate fixes the diagnosis enumerated were: weaken the server gate (would reopen the #1521 exposure), swallow the client error (mechanically impossible - Chromium emits the line for the failed resource, so no client catch can reach it), and widen the audit sweep's critical() filter (would edit a file inside three waves' frozen commandSequence, making it a contract-affecting change). The implemented fix touches none of those surfaces and instead restores an invariant the component already CLAIMED in its own header comment. The comment correction is therefore load-bearing, not decoration: the stale comment describing only the replica case is, by the diagnosis's own chain, why the second gate was never mirrored when #1521 added it.

`verify:qc:coop-campaign-journey` is in no workflow, so the client/server contract mismatch #1521 introduced on 2026-09-02 shipped with no CI signal and the last recorded green is 2026-07-06 (docs/qc/mekstation-qc-registry.json:1380 per the diagnosis). Both evidence files disclose this as D2 and both explicitly decline to close it. This review notes only that the disclosure is honest and that D2 is the reason this class of defect can recur silently; wiring it is out of scope for this PR and correctly left to the roadmap.
